name: Identification and valuation accuracy: agents better than a twenty-year appraiser
summary: I ran the agents' real code on the frozen copy (main-sync.gs lifted into node, the page driven in Chromium with stubbed model answers). The pipeline is built carefully. A comparable is kept only if a tool returned its link, a search page or a sale with no price shown never counts, a person's or an appraiser's figure is never overwritten, and an appraisal is flagged off the top of the range. But nothing measures accuracy and nothing defends a value to an attorney, so it is not yet better than a twenty-year appraiser. Three things put indefensible statements on papers today. When the server throws away every comparable the model invented, it keeps the figure and prints the model's "Four sold comparables at Christie's and Kodner… the median" beside "General estimate". A Court Inventory marked FINAL, with a signature block, counts a painting twice when the room check flagged the two lines as one object. The §20.2031-6(b) worklist tells counsel no expert appraisal is required, based on three unreviewed machine figures whose ranges add to $4,500. Several valuation settings relabel the paper without revaluing anything. Switching the basis to Replacement Value leaves Fair Market Value figures under the new heading. The §2032 tick dates the schedule to a day that has not come yet. Pasting a $1,100 WorthPoint sale turns a $4,200 agent figure into "WorthPoint comps $4,200" and marks it reviewed. The reader receives one word or one sentence per line, while the comparables, dates, range, confidence, reviewer and model stay on the desk. That falls short of the written explanation a beneficiary can ask for under §733.604, and the reader is never told the figures are estimates rather than appraisals. The confidence label is the model's own word: one 2019 eBay listing still reads "high". Review attention ignores the dollars at stake: a $20 box of books is marked unsure and a $9,000 chest is not. There is no feedback loop. An appraiser's figure deletes the agent's prediction, a desk rename keeps no record of Agent One's name, and realised sale prices are never compared with the figures. Nobody would know if a model upgrade made the values worse. The plan, in priority order: fix the three paper defects; make the three settings revalue or warn; give the papers a Valuation Support schedule and a disclosure sentence; enforce confidence and add a deep, two-model pass for high-dollar lines; then a scored golden set and a record of each prediction, so accuracy can be measured and the model upgrade gated on the score.
works_well: The server's evidence guard is real: a comparable is kept only when a tool result block returned its URL (_avSeenUrls reads result blocks only). Search and results pages and price-less sales are left out (_avResultsPage, AGENT_VALUE_NO_PRICE_RE). A research line with no sold comparable is relabelled General estimate at low confidence (gs1.js case A: 4 invented comps dropped, source General estimate, confidence low).

Agent One's prompt is strong on identification discipline. It states only what is readable and hedges inferences ('appears to be', 'in the style of'). A basis starting 'Read:' routes a line to research. The background, drawer and rubbish rules are clear, and a person or a recipient is never written into a name (main-sync.gs _agSystem).

Research requests carry what they should: the photograph, up to four close-ups, the room, the crew's note, the walkthrough room note, the other lines off the same photograph, and a 'Name checked by a person' mark (acc1 payload for s3: fileId f3, details fd1/fd0, the crew's note, alsoListed).
The general-lot ceiling works: in the 24-shot estate the $350 sofa and coffee tables were re-sent to research in the same run, not written as general figures (acc1: call 2 carried 4 re-sends).
Ownership of a figure is one rule (_avTakeValue, _avHasFigure): Agent Two never overwrites a typed or appraised figure, and Re-value replaces only its own.
invNeedsAppraisal reads the top of the agent's range, so a $2,500 to $4,000 range is flagged for appraisal whatever its point says (havellin.html:27886-27893).

Every estate figure is dated to the date of death and the prompt is told that date (acc1: valuationDate 2026-06-01 sent, valDate 2026-06-01 written). Schedules stamp how many values are unreviewed and stay DRAFT while any line is unvalued.
Whole dollars each on agent figures (agentValueWhole) keeps Each × Qty = Total exact, and the range is rounded the same way.
measurements: Agent One request per photograph (acc1.js, s.net): keys stableId, fileId, room, roomNote, fieldNote, details, listed. One main image at 900 px and JPEG 0.72 (_captureShot, havellin.html:40658), plus at most 4 close-ups at 1,200 px and 0.85. Crew note and room note are cut at 400 characters. No size, weight, serial, date of death or neighbouring photograph is sent.
Agent Two on a 24-shot probate estate (acc1.js): 2 calls. The first carried 24 items, 10 research and 14 ordinary. The second carried 4 ceiling re-sends at research (two sofas, two coffee tables).
Research depth for any line, whatever it may be worth: 5 web searches, 2 page fetches, effort medium, one model, one pass. An ordinary batch of 8 lots gets 8 searches (main-sync.gs:4127-4136).
Close-up order Agent Two receives: [fd1, fd0], newest first, for two close-ups the crew took fd0 then fd1 (acc1 payload). Agent One reads them oldest first (_agDetailRefs).

Court Inventory row (acc1/acc2): 4 columns (Description, Condition, a one-word Basis, FMV). 0 item numbers, 0 comparables, 0 per-line dates, 0 ranges, 0 confidence labels. Estate Inventory Report adds the basis sentence of at most about 20 words. 0 of 6 disclosure words ('Agent', 'automated', ' AI ', 'not an appraisal', 'not appraisals', 'estimates') appear on either paper (acc2.js).
TC types $650 over Agent Two's $220 (acc2 A): the $220 is gone, the stale range $100 to $300 stays, and the source is cleared so the paper reads 'not stated'.
Appraisal of $9,500 typed on a linked line (acc2 B): Agent Two's $4,200, its range, 2 comparables, confidence and lookup are all deleted. Nothing is kept to compare.

§20.2031-6(b) on a Form 706 estate (acc4.js): point figures total $2,800, ranges reach $4,500, 0 of 3 lines reviewed. The worklist prints 'does not require an expert appraisal to be filed with the return'.

FINAL Court Inventory (acc5.js): total $8,360 includes the $4,200 and $3,900 lines the room check flagged at high confidence as one painting. A signature block is present and the word 'duplicate' appears 0 times.

Use a WorthPoint sale at $1,100 on a $4,200 agent line (acc6.js): 0 dialogs. The figure stays $4,200, the source becomes WorthPoint comps, the line is marked reviewed, and the Court Inventory prints 'WorthPoint comps $4,200'.
Basis changed to Replacement Value (acc2 C): 0 dialogs, 0 new valuation calls, heading changed, the plates still $160.
§2032 tick on 2026-10-26 for a 2026-06-01 death (acc2 D): heading 'as of the alternate valuation date (Dec 1, 2026)'; 4 of 4 lines keep valDate 2026-06-01.
Confidence the server keeps (gs1.js): one 'sold' eBay listing dated 2019 stays 'high'. One comparable covering 12 plates, used for a line of 8, stays 'high'.
Count corrected on a researched set of 8 chairs to 6 (acc3.js): $2,400 becomes $1,800 and the range $1,600–$3,200 becomes $1,200–$2,400, with 0 re-valuation calls.
verifier_note: The ACC report holds up well. I reproduced every claim I could on my own scripts. I lifted the real server functions with the repo's brace matcher into gs-v.js. I drove the real desk controls in v1.js, v2.js and v2b.js, with the agents answered through the harness's stubbed Apps Script. Every paper and payload claim reproduced. My own runs found two siblings. First, on a partial drop (1 of 4 comparables kept) the line keeps source Auction comps and its basis still says 'Four sold comparables'. Second, a point value of $6,000 against a single kept sale at $900 stays 'high'. Where the report overstates, I have said so. The Court Inventory does say 'estimated fair market value', and its basis column separates appraisals from agent figures. The $9,000 chest is not unattended: on an estate it is flagged for appraisal (invNeedsAppraisal true). Four proposals run against Anthony's recorded rules. ACC-04's behaviour is the Domain rule for Use a WorthPoint sale. ACC-23's 'instead of rescaling' contradicts Each × Qty = Total. Half of ACC-03's proposal (counting unreviewed agent figures as unsettled) contradicts 'an unreviewed agent figure counts as valued'. ACC-06's gate on model upgrades contradicts the 2026-10-26 newest-model rule. I have marked these accordingly. I re-rated severities against the triage bar. Only the three paper defects (ACC-01, ACC-02, ACC-03) are fix-now candidates, and I kept ACC-03 at high: it is arithmetic on recorded values, but the paper does not say they are unreviewed. I could not test the legal readings: Treas. Reg. 20.2031-1(b), buyer's premium and the §733.604 written explanation.

findings.title: A figure built on invented comparables is kept, and its basis sentence still cites them on the paper
findings.where: Server: main-sync.gs _avLineResult (4697-4757; basis: _avClip(v.basis) at 4741, fmv kept whatever was dropped). App: havellin.html _avWrite 38674 (valNote = res.basis). Paper: printEstateInventoryReport itemRow (31055-31073).
findings.evidence: gs1.js (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/ACC/gs1.js): the real _avLineResult was given a $4,200 answer citing four Christie's/Kodner sales that no tool returned. It returned fmv 4200, confidence low, source General estimate, comps [], dropped 4, and the basis unchanged: 'Four sold comparables at Christie's and Kodner, 2025 to 2026; the median, less for a small tear.' acc6.js pushed that exact result through the real writer. The Estate Inventory Report row reads 'Oil on canvas harbor scene… Four sold comparables at Christie's and Kodner, 2025 to 2026; the median… $4,200 General estimate' (out/acc6.out).
findings.tc_impact: The TC sees a confident sentence and a figure and has no reason to doubt it. The attorney reads that four auction sales support $4,200, but none exist, and the figure itself was reasoned from them. A challenger who asks for the four sales finds nothing. This is exactly the 'never print a claim the app did not witness' failure.
findings.proposal: In _avLineResult, when comparables were dropped or unfit and no sold comparable survives, do not keep the model's basis. Either send the line back once as retry, with the note 'your comparables were not among the pages returned', or keep the figure with a server-written basis such as 'No sale the research could show; a best estimate from the kind of thing.' Also, whenever comparables were dropped, refuse a basis that names more sales than were kept (count digits and number words against kept.length). The app's _avWrite writes valNote only from that checked basis. The desk then shows unsure (already the case at low confidence) and the paper says 'general estimate' with an honest sentence.
findings.vnote: Server half: I lifted the real _avLineResult, _avSeenUrls and helpers myself. Given four Christie's comparables that no tool result returned, it gave fmv 4200, confidence low, source General estimate, 0 kept, 4 dropped, and the basis word for word: 'Four sold comparables at Christie's and Kodner, 2025 to 2026; the median.' New sibling: with 1 real comparable of 4, the line stays source 'Auction comps' at medium confidence, and the basis still says 'Four sold comparables'. App and paper half: that answer went through the real naming, room check and Agent Two pipeline (v1.js). _avWrite stored it as valNote (havellin.html:38674). The Estate Inventory Report row reads 'Oil on canvas harbor scene… Four sold comparables at Christie's and Kodner, 2025 to 2026; the median, less for a small tear … $4,200 General estimate'. The tool's own basis description models 'Four sold comparables, 2025 to 2026' (main-sync.gs:4235), so the model is prompted to cite counts. Spec §4b drops comparables but never touches the sentence.

findings.title: A FINAL, adoptable Court Inventory double counts a painting the room check flagged as one object
findings.where: printCourtInventory FINAL rule (havellin.html:34056, unvalued lines only), _invScheduleSection (33972); dupWith is read only on the desk (havellin.html:38034, 38083); printEstateInventoryReport; printTrustSchedule.
findings.evidence: acc5.js (out/acc5.out): every line is valued, and two lines carry a high-confidence room-check link ('The harbor painting: over the sofa in one, close up in the other.'). The desk shows Possible duplicates. The Court Inventory prints 'FINAL … Total tangible personal property (Fair Market Value): $8,360' with a signature block, and that total includes $4,200 and $3,900 for the same painting. 'duplicate' appears 0 times on the Court Inventory and the Estate Inventory Report.
findings.tc_impact: A TC who never opens the Possible duplicates panel, or sweeps it with Mark reviewed (only a flag), produces an adoptable schedule that overstates the estate by the duplicate's value. The PR signs it, and the attorney files an inventory with one painting listed twice. Agent Two also spends a research request valuing the duplicate.
findings.proposal: Treat an open possible duplicate (live, linked, no dupOK) like an unvalued line on every valued paper. The schedule stays DRAFT with '1 possible double count not yet decided: #1 and #2 (the harbor painting)', the signature block is withheld, and the IN PROGRESS stamp on the Estate Inventory Report names the pair. In agentValueAuto, hold back the later line of a high-confidence pair until a person presses Remove or Not duplicates, so Agent Two does not research the same object twice.
findings.decided_conflict: Auto-merging possible duplicate lines stays ruled out: this only withholds FINAL and names the pair.
findings.vnote: The full pipeline ran through the real controls: Name 4 shots pressed, the room check answering a high-confidence double [s0, s1], then Agent Two by itself. Both paintings went to research ('s0:comps,s1:comps'), so the duplicate is researched twice. The desk shows Possible duplicates. The Court Inventory, opened from More ▾ in the viewer, reads 'FINAL · 4 values not yet reviewed'. Its total is $8,360, which includes both $4,200 and $3,900, with the signature block present and no mention of a duplicate. The EIR is IN PROGRESS and also never mentions the pair. grep finds dupWith read only on the desk (havellin.html:38034, 38083) and in its writer. The proposal withholds FINAL and does not merge, so it stays within 'flag, never merge'.

findings.fixed: 2026-10-27 (P7, its critical part: CLAUDE.md, the §20.2031-6(b) aggregate tells the truth; tests/p7-evidence.test.js, browser step 121)
findings.title: §20.2031-6(b) 'does not require an expert appraisal' is concluded from unreviewed agent point figures
findings.where: maivAggregate (havellin.html:28104, reads fmv only) and maivStatement_; the worklist sentence in printAppraisalWorklist; compare invNeedsAppraisal (27886-27893), which reads valHigh on an agent figure.
findings.evidence: acc4.js (out/acc4.out): a Form 706 estate with three art lines valued by Agent Two at $900, $950 and $950 (ranges $500 to $1,500 each), none reviewed and none flagged for appraisal. The worklist prints: '3 articles of marked artistic or intrinsic value total $2,800, under the $3,000 aggregate … Below the $3,000 aggregate, so §20.2031-6(b) does not require an expert appraisal to be filed with the return.' The agent's own high ends add to $4,500.
findings.tc_impact: The worklist hands counsel a legal conclusion, no sworn expert appraisal needed with the 706, based on three machine guesses nobody has looked at. If the art is really worth $4,000, the return goes in without the appraisal the regulation requires. The per-line appraisal rule is cautious (it reads the top of the range), and this aggregate is not, so the two disagree.
findings.proposal: In maivAggregate, read an agent figure (valuedBy agent) at its valHigh, the same rule as invNeedsAppraisal, and count an unreviewed agent figure as unsettled. Have maivStatement_ say: 'Agent Two's estimates total $2,800, and its ranges reach $4,500: the $3,000 aggregate may be crossed. Review these lines or have the class appraised.' Print 'does not require' only once every MAIV line carries a reviewed or appraised figure and the ranges stay under the threshold.
findings.vnote: On a 706 probate (gate706 yes) I pressed Value 4 lines. Agent Two returned $900, $950 and $950, each ranged $500–$1,500, none reviewed and none flagged for appraisal. The Appraisal Worklist, from More ▾ in the viewer, prints: '3 articles … total $2,800, under the $3,000 aggregate … Below the $3,000 aggregate, so §20.2031-6(b) does not require an expert appraisal to be filed with the return.' The worklist carries no unreviewed stamp. maivAggregate reads fmv only (havellin.html:28104), while invNeedsAppraisal reads valHigh, so the two rules disagree. Re-rated from fix-now to high: the conclusion is arithmetic on recorded values, but it is printed with no warning that they are unreviewed machine figures. The worklist also goes in the estate package. Caution on the proposal: reading an agent figure at valHigh mirrors invNeedsAppraisal and is fine. 'Count an unreviewed agent figure as unsettled' contradicts the Domain rule 'An unreviewed agent figure counts as valued' (CLAUDE.md, Agent Two's figures). The rule-compatible fix is to read valHigh and add the _avUnreviewedStamp warning to this sentence.

findings.title: Use a WorthPoint sale relabels Agent Two's figure as 'WorthPoint comps' even when the sale contradicts it
findings.where: agentValueUseSale (havellin.html:39086-39110): the figure is written only when the line has none, but valSource is always set and the line is stamped reviewed; browser step 69 pins 'the figure stays the person's to change'.
findings.evidence: acc6.js (out/acc6.out): through the record's real form, a $1,100 sale was pasted on a bronze Agent Two valued at $4,200 from two sold comparables. Result: fmv 4200, source WorthPoint comps, valNote still 'Two sold comparables, 2025; the median.', reviewed true, 0 dialogs. The Court Inventory row reads 'Bronze figure of a dancer… WorthPoint comps $4,200'.
findings.tc_impact: The TC did the right thing (checked WorthPoint) and expected the figure to follow. Instead the paper now tells the attorney that a WorthPoint comparable supports $4,200 when the comparable says $1,100, and the line is marked reviewed, so nothing brings it back.
findings.proposal: When a sale is pasted on a line with a figure, ask once: 'Use $1,100 as the value? (OK) Keep $4,200 and file the sale as a comparable only? (Cancel)'. OK writes the figure, valuedBy desk and a basis like 'WorthPoint sale, 2026-03-02: $1,100'. Cancel keeps the source as it was and only adds the comparable. Skip the question when the sale is within 15% of the figure. Never set 'WorthPoint comps' over a figure the pasted sale does not support.
findings.vnote: Reproduced through the record's real form (Use a WorthPoint sale, $1,100) on a $9,000 Agent Two line. 0 dialogs. Afterwards fmv 9000, valSource 'WorthPoint comps', valNote still 'Sold comparables.', valuedBy still 'agent', the line reviewed, and the $1,100 comparable first. This is exactly the Domain rule: 'Use a WorthPoint sale (agentValueUseSale) puts a pasted sale first in the comparables, names WorthPoint comps … and reviews the line, its value with it; a line with no figure takes the sale's price' (CLAUDE.md, Agent Two's figures; AGENT_TWO_SPEC §4a). The case to revisit it is strong: the paper then says WorthPoint supports a figure the sale contradicts. That is Anthony's call, posed as a question.

findings.title: An appraiser's figure erases the agent's prediction, and a TC's correction keeps no record of it: nothing to learn from
findings.where: _avTakeValue (havellin.html:38752-38772): the appraisal arm deletes every AGENT_VALUE_OWN field; the desk arm drops valSource and valNote and overwrites fmv; AGENT_VALUE_OWN (38611).
findings.evidence: acc2.js (out/acc2.out). Painting: after Agent Two, {fmv 4200, valLow 3000, valHigh 5500, valConf medium, 2 comps}. After the appraiser was linked and $9,500 typed, only {fmv 9500, valSource Appraisal, valuedBy appraiser}. Sofa: after the TC typed $650 over $220, the $220 is gone and the stale range $100 to $300 stays.
findings.tc_impact: Every appraisal and every correction is ground truth about the agent: what an ASA appraiser says the item is worth against what the agent said. Today that signal is destroyed the moment it arrives, so Havellin can never say 'our agent is within 20% of our appraisers on 80% of lines', which is the claim that would win a trust officer.
findings.proposal: Before _avTakeValue clears anything, archive the agent's answer once: valAgent = {fmv, low, high, conf, source, mode, model, backend, at, nameAt}. Keep it sticky, on the savePhotoRefs list, never printed, and dropped only by a removal. Do the same when the desk types over an agent figure. Then add a Closing-bar line for each job ('Agent Two against 6 appraisals: median error 18%, 5 of 6 inside its range') that feeds the accuracy programme (ACC-06).
findings.vnote: Typed $650 into the row's Total box over Agent Two's $20 (v2.js). Result: fmv 650, valuedBy desk, valConf gone, the agent's $20 gone. The stale range 10–30, valComps and valNameAt stay. Code: the appraisal arm of _avTakeValue deletes every AGENT_VALUE_OWN field, and on an agent figure valNote too (havellin.html:38752-38772). The proposal archives the prediction in an unprinted field. That does not contradict §2.3's 'the agent's fields go', since they still go from what prints. Re-rated from high to medium: this is a measurement gap with nothing wrong on any paper.

findings.title: No measurement of the agents' accuracy, and the model upgrades itself with no evaluation gate
findings.where: testAgentIdentify (main-sync.gs:3676), testAgentRoomCheck (4055), testAgentValue (4922-4962): four probes with no expected answers; _agNewestOf and _agModelList (3087-3120) choose the newest model; nothing in havellin.html or the specs mentions golden, calibration or accuracy (grep).
findings.evidence: grep -i 'golden|calibrat|accuracy|MAPE' over havellin.html, main-sync.gs and both agent specs finds nothing about the agents. testAgentValue only logs figures for Herend plates, flatware, books and a mirror, with no truth to compare against. The spec's test plan (AGENT_TWO_SPEC.md §10) is all unit tests and stubs.
findings.tc_impact: Anthony wants agents that identify and value better than anyone, and today nobody can tell whether they do, whether a prompt change helped, or whether the next model silently made values worse. A trust officer who asks how accurate the values are gets no answer.
findings.proposal: Build a golden set: 60 to 100 real items photographed the Havellin way, with Drive file ids and known truth. Sources: Havellin's own consignments realised at Kodner (hammer plus premium), appraisers' figures from Havellin jobs (ACC-05), and public lot pages with realised prices across the categories. Add testAgentGolden(), run from the editor, which names and values the set and writes a row to an AgentScores tab. Score identification (category exact; maker, material and medium by a short checklist per item) and value (median absolute percentage error overall and by category, share of truths inside low to high, signed bias, and error by confidence bucket, with the expectation that high beats medium beats low). Run it on every BACKEND_VERSION and whenever _agModelList finds a new model. A new model becomes the first choice only once its logged score is at least the current one's.
findings.decided_conflict: 'Which model, for every agent call' (Anthony, 2026-10-26: newest model so they are always the most accurate). This keeps the auto-upgrade and makes 'most accurate' measured rather than assumed.
findings.vnote: grep for golden, calibrat or MAPE finds 0 hits in main-sync.gs and both agent specs. The 3 hits in havellin.html are unrelated (pricing and phone-read comments). The three testAgent* probes (main-sync.gs:3676, 4055, 4922) only log answers, with no expected values to compare against. Open work only says 'tune … on the first real estate', so this is not a duplicate. Caution: the half of the proposal that makes a new model the first choice only once it scores as well contradicts Anthony's 2026-10-26 rule ('make sure the agents update the model when there are new models', 'Which model, for every agent call'). Build the golden set and the score; put the gate to Anthony as a question.

findings.title: The papers carry no evidence: comparables, dates, range, confidence, method and reviewer stay on the desk
findings.where: _invScheduleSection (havellin.html:33972-33997, one word through invValBasisWord); printEstateInventoryReport itemRow (31055); valComps is read only by _avPanelHtml (39280); valConf, valLow/valHigh and valReviewedBy are printed nowhere.
findings.evidence: acc2.js (out/acc2.out): the Court Inventory and Estate Inventory Report contain none of the comparable venues or links, no range, no confidence and no per-line date. The Court Inventory's Basis column reads 'auction comps' or 'general estimate' (out/acc1-court-inventory.html).
findings.tc_impact: The research exists (up to six comparables with venue, date, price, sold or asking, and a link), but the attorney cannot see it. A beneficiary entitled under §733.604 to a written explanation of how each value was determined gets one word. A challenger cannot reproduce a figure, so the work is no more defensible than a spreadsheet's.
findings.proposal: Add a Valuation Support schedule: under More ▾, filed with the package after the ledger, and filterable to one beneficiary's lines. Build it from fields already on each line: item number, thumbnail and description; value with its range; standard and date; method (sold comparables, going rate for that kind of lot, appraisal by a named appraiser, or a figure set by a named person); the comparables table (venue, date, price, sold or asking, link); the adjustment sentence; confidence; reviewed by and on; model and backend version. Open with a one-page methodology statement (who values, the standard under Treas. Reg. 20.2031-1(b), the date, that these are not USPAP appraisals, and the referral threshold). No new work for the TC.
findings.vnote: The Court Inventory I captured from the viewer carries no venue, comparable, range or confidence. Its row is Description, Condition, a one-word Basis, FMV. valComps is read only by the desk record (_avPanelHtml, havellin.html:39280) and the save list; nothing in saveInventory.gs reads comps, range or confidence. The data exists on each line, so the gap is presentation only. The §733.604 written-explanation point is a sound legal reading I cannot test here.

findings.title: The valued schedules never say who made the figures, or that they are estimates and not appraisals; the release request does
findings.where: printApprovalRequest (havellin.html:32551: 'Values are Havellin's estimates as of the date shown and are not appraisals unless an appraisal is noted against the line'); printDonationRecord (34801) says the same; printCourtInventory, printEstateInventoryReport and printTrustSchedule say nothing of the kind.
findings.evidence: acc2.js: none of 'Agent', 'automated', ' AI ', 'not an appraisal', 'not appraisals' or 'estimates' appears in the Estate Inventory Report or Court Inventory html (out/acc2-eir-avd.html, out/acc2-ci-avd.html). The Court Inventory's footer reads only 'Values are estimated fair market value as of date of death.'
findings.tc_impact: Counsel reading the schedule that matters most can take Agent Two's machine figures for an appraiser's. The two papers that carry the figures disagree with the one that releases the property about what the figures are.
findings.proposal: Make one constant, INV_VALUE_DISCLOSURE: 'Values are Havellin's estimates of fair market value as of <date>, researched against sold comparables where they exist, and are not appraisals unless an appraisal is named against the line.' Print it under the basis line of every valued paper and the workbook header, and add it to COUNSEL_REVIEW_BUNDLE.md.
findings.vnote: Measured: neither the Court Inventory nor the EIR carries 'not an appraisal', 'not appraisals', 'Agent' or 'automated'. The CI footer reads 'Values are estimated fair market value as of date of death.' The release request (havellin.html:32551) and the Donation Record (34801) both say the values are Havellin's estimates and not appraisals, so the papers disagree. Overstatement in the report: the CI does say 'estimated', and its Basis column distinguishes 'appraisal · <name>' from 'auction comps' and 'general estimate'. The estate agreement also says the Project Records 'are not an appraisal or a statement of value' (54365). Re-rated from high to medium.

The EIR reads 'as of the alternate valuation date (Dec 1, 2026)', a future day, and so does the CI. findings.fixed: 2026-10-27, the first half only (P7: an Etsy, 1stDibs, Chairish, Ruby Lane, Replacements or retail-store comparable is always asking; the confidence ceiling is not built)
findings.title: Confidence is the model's own word: one old listing, or a comparable for a different lot size, stays 'high'
findings.where: _avLineResult (main-sync.gs:4697-4757): only a dropped comparable lowers confidence, and only the absence of a sold one forces low; the comparable schema has no quantity or market field (_avTool comps, 4285-4300).
findings.evidence: gs1.js (out/gs1.out) case B: one 'sold' eBay /itm/ page dated 2019-03, for a 2026-06-01 valuation date, kept confidence 'high' and source Online comps. Case C: one sold comparable covering twelve plates, for a line of eight, kept 'high'. The prompt defines high as 'several close sold comparables agree', but nothing counts them.
findings.tc_impact: The row's unsure hint (invLineUnsure) and the TC's trust both ride on that word. A single stale sale earns the same 'high' as five recent matched ones, so the TC skims lines that most need a look, and the attorney's reviewer has no way to tell.
findings.proposal: Make the server set the confidence ceiling. High needs at least 3 kept sold comparables dated within 3 years of the valuation date, with the point value between their lowest and highest. Medium needs at least 1 sold within 5 years. Anything else is low. Add units (articles the listing covered) and market (international auction, regional auction, online auction, marketplace sold, retail resale, asking) to the comparable schema. Compute the per-unit median of the kept sold comparables, store it, and lower confidence one level when the point is more than 50% away from it with no stated reason.
findings.vnote: Reproduced on the lifted server function. One kept 'sold' eBay /itm/ listing dated 2019-03 comes back 'high', source Online comps. New sibling: a point value of $6,000 against its single kept sale at $900 also stays 'high'. Only a dropped comparable lowers confidence, and only the absence of any sold one forces low (main-sync.gs:4730-4733). The comparable schema is title, venue, saleDate, price, url, kind, with no quantity, market or premium. Re-rated from high to medium: confidence prints on no paper today, and it drives only the desk's unsure hint.

findings.title: The standard of value in Agent Two's prompt says 'not retail' and is silent on buyer's premium
findings.where: _avSystem, WHAT A VALUE MEANS HERE (main-sync.gs:4342-4351: 'In practice it is what the thing actually SELLS for on the secondary market: auction prices realised and completed sales. It is not retail…'); THE TWO DEPTHS (4395-4404).
findings.evidence: out/av-system-fmv.txt (the prompt as built). gs1.js: /premium/i on the FMV prompt is false. Treas. Reg. 20.2031-1(b) values an item in the market in which it is most commonly sold to the public, taking its location into account, and at retail for items the public generally buys at retail (the regulation's used-car example). The prompt's blanket 'not retail' and its default to auction prices realised can systematically understate, for instance used furniture whose public market is consignment or resale retail. Hammer prices and all-in eBay prices get mixed with no rule. (The regulation is quoted from memory; counsel to confirm its use here.)
findings.tc_impact: On a Form 706 estate an understated figure costs the beneficiaries their stepped-up basis and invites a challenge, and the prompt's own estate paragraph warns against understatement. A senior appraiser names the market and whether the premium is in. Today the reader cannot tell, and two lines can be valued on different footings.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the paragraph: value each line in the market where such an item is most commonly sold to the public, located where appropriate (Palm Beach County regionally for bulky things, nationally for small valuable ones), naming that market in the basis sentence; for an auction comparable use the price the buyer paid (hammer plus buyer's premium), adding the house's stated premium when a page shows hammer only. Usual estate practice; the appraiser and counsel to confirm. Add premium (included, added, unknown) to the comparable schema, and add the sentence to COUNSEL_REVIEW_BUNDLE.md.
findings.vnote: Prompt text verified on the lifted _avSystem: the FMV paragraph includes 'It is not retail'; 'premium' does not appear; 'most commonly sold' does not appear. The conflict with Treas. Reg. 20.2031-1(b)'s market-most-commonly-sold and retail rule, and the buyer's-premium question, are sound expert judgements I cannot test here; counsel and an appraiser should confirm them. Mitigation that lowers severity: the research section already sends branded furniture to 'resale and consignment sales', which is the secondhand retail market. So the error is the blanket phrase and the silence on hammer-vs-premium, not every value. Re-rated from high to medium.

findings.title: Review attention ignores the dollars at stake: a $20 box of books is 'unsure' and a $9,000 chest is not
findings.where: invLineUnsure (havellin.html:37245-37253) reads only the confidence word; the Unsure chip in the work bar.
findings.evidence: acc3.js (out/acc3.out): s4 'Box of paperback novels' $20, low confidence: unsure true. s5 'Painted pine blanket chest, appears 19th century' $9,000 (range $4,000 to $14,000), medium confidence: unsure false. The three art lines at $900 to $950, medium confidence: not unsure.
findings.tc_impact: On a 400-line house the TC works Unsure first, as the desk guide says, and spends the evening on cheap guesses while a $10,000-wide range goes by under one tick. The discerning reader cares about the dollars, not the count of guesses.
findings.proposal: Order the Unsure chip, and the rows it filters, by dollars at risk (valHigh − valLow). Mark unsure any line whose range width is $1,000 or more whatever the model says, and send those lines to the deep pass in ACC-14 automatically, before the TC sees them. This adds no review step and no badge on ordinary lines.
findings.decided_conflict: Touches 'A second review of Agent Two's figures … or an agent's badge on every line it touched' only to the extent that it widens the existing unsure hint to high-dollar ranges; there is still one tick and no new pile.
findings.vnote: Driven: the $20 books at low confidence are unsure, and the $9,000 chest (range $4,000–$14,000, medium) is not. The Unsure chip reads 'Unsure 1'. invLineUnsure reads only the confidence word (havellin.html:37245-37253). Overstated, though: on an estate the chest is flagged for appraisal (invNeedsAppraisal true in my run, reading the top of the range), and a living job gets the 'worth a specialist' notice. So high-dollar lines already get attention by another path. The gap is wide ranges below the appraisal threshold. Widening the existing hint adds no tier, so it stays within the 'one review' rule.

findings.title: Every line gets the same shallow research and a single opinion, whatever it may be worth
findings.where: agentValueMode (havellin.html:38465, only 'comps' or 'general'); AGENT_VALUE_SEARCHES {comps 5, general 8}, AGENT_VALUE_FETCHES 2, AGENT_VALUE_EFFORT 'medium' (main-sync.gs:4127-4136); _agModels('value') chooses one model.
findings.evidence: The research depth is identical for a $40 vase and a $20,000 painting: 5 searches, 2 page fetches, effort medium, one model, one pass. An ordinary batch of 8 lots gets more searches (8) than a research line (5). Open work already notes that two fetches limit how many sale pages can be read.
findings.tc_impact: The lines that decide most of an estate's total get the least scrutiny relative to their stakes, and there is no second opinion to catch a misattribution or a wrong market. That is where a twenty-year appraiser beats the agent today.
findings.proposal: Add a third depth, 'deep', in agentValueMode. It applies when the first figure's high end is $1,000 or more, or to an intrinsic line at low confidence, and always on an estate line above invAppraisalThreshold/3. Settings: effort high, 10 searches, 6 fetches, run independently on both models (first choice and fallback). Combine on the server: figures within 25% give the median and keep the higher confidence; a wider gap gives low confidence plus an 'appraiser' notice naming both figures. Send deep lines one to a request at a lower parallel width so each fits UrlFetchApp's limit, or through the Message Batches API collected when the desk next opens (check in the editor that batches accept the web tools). Measure it on the golden set (ACC-06) before turning it on.
findings.vnote: The constants are as described: AGENT_VALUE_SEARCHES {comps 5, general 8}, AGENT_VALUE_FETCHES 2, AGENT_VALUE_EFFORT 'medium' (main-sync.gs:4127-4136), and agentValueMode answers only comps or general. Imprecision: the 8 general searches are a cap shared across a batch of 8 lots, not 8 per lot. Not a duplicate: Open work only notes raising AGENT_VALUE_FETCHES and the Q60 generic-lot card. Nothing on the Decided list blocks it. Re-rated from high to medium: the benefit is unmeasured until a golden set exists (ACC-06).

findings.title: Agent Two reads the newest four close-ups while the field guide tells the crew 'most important first: the app only reads the first four'
findings.where: invLineCloseUps (havellin.html:40794-40803, sorts by ts descending); _agDetailRefs (37570, ascending); photography-guide.html:480-481.
findings.evidence: acc1.js payload (out/acc1-agent-bodies.json): the crew took the painting's close-ups fd0 then fd1, and Agent Two was sent [fd1, fd0]. On a painting with six close-ups (signature first, as the guide asks), Agent Two would miss the signature and read the last four, while Agent One read the first four.
findings.tc_impact: The crew follows the guide and puts the signature first, and the valuer never sees it, so the line is priced as an unsigned harbour scene.
findings.proposal: One order for both agents: close-ups added at the desk first (they answer a Look at this), then the field's close-ups in the order taken, four at most. Mark desk-added close-ups at capture (invAddCloseUp) so the sort can tell them apart, and keep the guide's sentence true.

Agent One's _agDetailRefs sorts oldest first. The photography guide says 'Most important first: the app only reads the first four' (photography-guide.html:480-481), which is true only of Agent One.

findings.title: The value drivers an appraiser records are never captured or sent: size, weight, solid-or-plated stamps, reference numbers, and a method per category
findings.where: _avItemPayload (havellin.html:38570, no serial, dimensions or weight); _avSystem has no per-category method; photography-guide.html (the kit is two cloths, and 'Say the size' covers paintings and rugs only).
findings.evidence: acc1 payload keys: stableId, mode, name, category, qty, condition, conditionChecked, fieldNote, agentBasis, nameChecked, categoryChecked, room, roomNote, photoNote, alsoListed, fileId, details. The line's serial column (INVENTORY_COLUMNS 'serial') is not sent. gs1.js: weight, troy ounces, melt and spot price appear nowhere in the prompt. grep of photography-guide.html: no tape measure, scale, loupe, flashlight or scale card in the kit.
findings.tc_impact: Sterling hollowware and gold are floored by weight. A 9×12 rug and a 3×5 rug, or a 40-inch canvas and a 10-inch one, differ several times over. '14K GF' is not gold. A watch's reference number sets its price. Without these facts the agent prices the generic thing, and an appraiser with a loupe and a scale outperforms it.
findings.proposal: Field: add a tape measure, a gram kitchen scale, a clip-on macro lens or loupe, a flashlight for raking light, and a printed scale card placed in item photographs of art, rugs and silver. The guide says to state the size and the weight. Agent One: read dimensions off the scale card into the name, and never name gold or sterling over a GF, GE, HGE, RGP, EPNS or 'plate' stamp. Agent Two: append a short notes block for the line's category to the research user turn (so the cached system prompt is unaffected). Silver: weighted or solid, melt as a floor at troy ounces × spot on the valuation date where a weight is given. Jewelry: gemstones are never graded from a photograph, so raise an appraiser notice above a threshold. Art: original-or-print evidence, size, the artist's sold record. Rugs: size, knot, origin, condition. Watches and instruments: reference and serial. Wine: producer, vintage, fill. Send serial on any line that is not a firearm.
findings.vnote: The payload keys I captured from the real request are stableId, mode, name, category, qty, condition, conditionChecked, fieldNote, agentBasis, nameChecked, categoryChecked, room, roomNote, photoNote, alsoListed, fileId and details. No serial is sent. The Agent Two prompt has no weight, troy, melt or spot rule and no plated-metal rule (gs-v.js). The field kit is two cloths (photography-guide.html:630-631). Agent One already writes a size the crew says into the name (main-sync.gs:3415-3420). Nothing on the Decided list blocks the proposal, but each new field step must pass CLAUDE.md's 'what it costs the concierge on a full house'.

findings.title: Agent One's 'mark too small to read' reaches only the evening desk, after the crew has left the house
findings.where: agentNotices readers are all on the desk (havellin.html:37339, 37882-37908, 39478); agentNameShots is called only from the work bar button (39375); nothing in the Job Plan or the camera reads them.
findings.evidence: grep 'agentNotices' over havellin.html: every reader is on the desk. Naming starts only when someone presses Name N shots on Job Admin & Inv, so a Look at this about a blurred hallmark is raised hours after the last photograph, and + Close-up at the desk can only use what is already in the iPad's photos.
findings.tc_impact: The TC finds out at 9 pm that eight marks were unreadable, and either returns to the house or lets the lines go out priced as generic. The best close-up is the one taken while the crew is still standing in front of the piece.
findings.proposal: Name each room's Items photographs as they reach Drive: an automatic agentNameShots for that room when the camera closes or after a room's batch uploads, when online. Then draw a Close-ups wanted list on the room's brief and in the camera: the line's thumbnail, Agent One's reason, and one press arming Close-up on that line. Field mode hides the desk (CLAUDE.md Screens). So a Look at this about a blurred mark is first seen at the desk. Not on the Decided list and not in Open work.

findings.title: Nothing learns from corrections, realised prices or the job's own confirmed makers
findings.where: _invEdit (havellin.html, key objectName: namedBy set to desk and Agent One's name overwritten); dispositionLedger (34374) sums gross and never compares it with fmv; _agContext (37616) and _avContext (38532) carry no job-level hints.
findings.evidence: Code reading: a desk rename keeps no copy of Agent One's name (valNameFrom covers Agent Two's renames only). Proceeds statements record each sold line's gross, but no function reads gross beside fmv (grep 'fmv' with 'gross' finds only the column readers at 29355, 29737, 40309). Neither agent is told what the desk has already confirmed on the same job, for example Herend Rothschild Bird on the plates.
findings.tc_impact: The TC teaches the agents the same correction fifty times in one house (the pattern, the brand), and Havellin never builds the Palm Beach sold-price knowledge that would let it beat a spreadsheet appraiser.
findings.proposal: Keep agentName and agentCat (Agent One's first answer, immutable, on the save list). Build jobMakerHints(jobId) from names a person typed and appraisers' reports, for example 'This house: Herend Rothschild Bird, Gorham Chantilly, Restoration Hardware', and send it in both agents' job context. Add a realised-against-estimate readout per sold line (gross including premium against fmv) on the Closing bar, and pool it across jobs into Havellin's own comparables, which Agent Two can be given as evidence for that kind of item.
findings.vnote: _invEdit on objectName sets namedBy desk and deletes agentConf, with no copy of the old name (havellin.html:29764-29767). valNameFrom exists only when Agent Two renamed the line, and valNameAt holds the name the figure was made under, so the history is partial. No code compares a sold line's gross with its fmv: the only readers are the column formatters at 29355, 29737 and 40309. Neither agent's context carries job-level maker hints. The proposal does not conflict with any decided rule.

findings.title: A figure does not record which model, prompt version or depth made it
findings.where: agentValueLines sets r.model (main-sync.gs:4893), but _avWrite (havellin.html:38629-38677) writes no model, backend version or mode; Agent One's answer model is likewise not stored (_agWrite 37631).
findings.evidence: grep 'valModel|agentModel|res.model' over havellin.html finds nothing. _agDemote and the fallback can move a task to Opus for six hours, so one estate can be valued half by Fable 5.1 and half by Opus 5.5 with no trace on the lines.
findings.tc_impact: If a value is challenged, Havellin cannot say what produced it. Nor can it re-run the same pipeline, or tell after a model change which lines to revalue.
findings.proposal: Write valModel, valBackend (BACKEND_VERSION, echoed in the answer) and valMode on each line from _avWrite, and agentModel from _agWrite, all on the save list. Print them on the Valuation Support schedule (ACC-07), and offer 'Re-value the N lines made by an earlier model' after a backend change.
findings.vnote: grep for valModel, agentModel or valBackend in havellin.html finds nothing. _avWrite writes no model, version or mode (havellin.html:38629-38677), although the server sets r.model on each result (main-sync.gs:4893). Spec §5's field table lists no model either.

findings.title: The Court Inventory and Trust Schedule rows carry no item number, so the filed schedule cannot be tied to its photographs or appraisals
findings.where: _invScheduleSection (havellin.html:33972-33997: Description, Condition, Basis, FMV); the comment in printAppraisalWorklist says the item number is 'the one the Court Inventory and the receipts cite'.
findings.evidence: acc1.js (out/acc1-court-inventory.html): no row carries a number. Two 'Oil on canvas harbor scene…' rows and two '— as photographed not stated —' rows cannot be told apart, and the only numbers on the page are in the floor sentence ('#8 unnamed, #20 unnamed').
findings.tc_impact: Counsel cannot match a filed line to the photograph, the appraisal report, the release request or a beneficiary's receipt, all of which use the item number. Two lines with the same name look like a duplicate.
findings.proposal: Add a Ref column (the permanent item number, via _invAssignItemNos) as the first column of _invScheduleSection, as the Estate Inventory Report already does.
findings.vnote: The Court Inventory captured from the viewer has no item number or Ref header. My test for '\bRef\b|#1|Item #' was false. _invScheduleSection builds Description, Condition, Basis, FMV only (havellin.html:33972-33997). The Estate Inventory Report does carry Ref (_invItemNo, 31059).

findings.title: An ordinary batch of eight trusts the model's line labels: a swapped answer renames and values the wrong line
findings.where: agentValueLines (main-sync.gs:4879-4893: answers keyed by the model's 'line' label); _avRename (havellin.html:38693) writes the returned name over an unreviewed Agent One name, including on text-only ordinary lots.
findings.evidence: Code reading: nothing checks that the answer given for L3 is about L3's name. The prompt allows a rename on a text-only ordinary lot 'unless it is plainly wrong', so if L3's and L4's answers are swapped, the platter line is renamed and valued as the lamp.
findings.tc_impact: A silent swap puts the right words and figure on the wrong photograph, and nothing on the desk would show it.
findings.proposal: Add a required given field to record_values: the first five words of the name it was sent. The server drops an entry whose given does not match its line's name and returns that line as retry. On a text-only ordinary lot, accept a rename only if it keeps the head noun.
findings.vnote: Code verified: agentValueLines maps each answer to its line only by the model's 'line' label (byLine[v.line], main-sync.gs:4879-4893), with no check that the name returned matches the line sent. _avRename then writes the returned name over an unreviewed Agent One name. Whether a model actually swaps labels in a batch of 8 can only be seen against the live model, and I did not observe it.

findings.title: Agent Two's only evidence is the open web; licensed and Havellin-owned sources are not used
findings.where: _avTools (main-sync.gs, web_search_20260209 and web_fetch_20260209 only); AGENT_TWO_SPEC.md §4 (WorthPoint by hand; eBay sold data closed; LiveAuctioneers and Invaluable only through search).
findings.evidence: Spec §4 and the code: every comparable comes from a public web search, and the first live testAgentValue cited a search page and a price-results page (Open work, 2026-10-26b). Regional houses' realised prices, which are the Palm Beach market, show up only if search happens to surface them.
findings.tc_impact: The appraiser with twenty years has a subscription database and the local houses' results. Without them the agent is anchored on whatever pages search returns, and those are often asking prices or other markets.
findings.proposal: By agreement, never by scraping (the Decided rule stands): (1) Havellin's own realised results (ACC-18) as a first source, sent as text comparables for the same kind of item. (2) A data-sharing arrangement with one or two regional houses (Kodner and a Palm Beach house) for realised results by category, given to Agent Two as evidence the server provides. (3) A licensed price database for art and artists if one licenses API access, and WorthPoint partner access as the spec anticipates (§4a). Score each source on the golden set before relying on it.
findings.decided_conflict: Browser automation of WorthPoint and scraping LiveAuctioneers or Invaluable stay ruled out; these are licensed feeds and partnerships.
findings.vnote: Accurate. The tools are web_search and web_fetch only, and AGENT_TWO_SPEC §4 rules out WorthPoint automation and scraping LiveAuctioneers or Invaluable, while anticipating WorthPoint partner access (§4a). The proposal is licensed feeds and partnerships, which the Decided list leaves open. This is a business arrangement more than a desk fix, so low for the desk plan.

findings.title: Correcting the count on a researched set rescales linearly, and sets are not linear
findings.where: _invQtyCarriesValue (havellin.html:29561-29570).
findings.evidence: KNOWN (Open work, 2026-10-25b: a count change rescales the figure and range but not the comparables); new impact here. acc3.js: a researched set of eight Chippendale-style chairs at $2,400 was changed to 6 and became $1,800 (range $1,200 to $2,400), with 0 revaluation calls and the basis 'Sold comparables.' unchanged. A full set of eight sells for more per chair than six.
findings.tc_impact: A count correction on a set, the commonest desk edit on a dining room, quietly misprices the set.
findings.proposal: On a research line, meaning an intrinsic category or a set, treat a count change like a rename: send it to Agent Two through the agentValueAfterRename path (call it agentValueAfterQty) instead of rescaling. Keep the linear rescale for ordinary lots.
findings.vnote: Reproduced on the row's real Qty box: researched chairs went from 8 at $2,400 to 6 at $1,800, the range from $1,600–$3,200 to $1,200–$2,400, with 0 valuation calls and the basis unchanged. The rescale itself is the Domain rule 'Each × Qty = Total (2026-10-25b) … a count changed carries Each across (_invQtyCarriesValue, the agent's range with it)'. The comparables part is already known (Open work: 'a count changed rescales an agent figure and its range but not its comparables'). The proposal's 'instead of rescaling' contradicts Anthony's 'the math should happen automatically'. A compatible version would rescale at once and then queue a research Re-value, as agentValueAfterRename does.

findings.title: The Value and Re-value confirmations promise 'researched against sold comparables' where the outcome may be a general estimate
findings.where: agentValueRun's confirm (havellin.html:38808-38812) and agentRevalue's confirm (38829); the planner's sibling is the Name N shots confirm (37748: 'Nothing is valued').
findings.evidence: acc2.js dialog: 'Value 4 lines on this job? 2 researched against sold comparables, 2 valued as everyday lots.' In acc6, a researched line with no surviving sold comparable came back as General estimate. The count is also taken before the $250-per-article ceiling re-sends lines (acc1: 4 more lines were researched).
findings.tc_impact: The words promise more evidence than some lines will carry, and the TC has no reason to look at them.
findings.proposal: Say 'N researched (sold comparables where they can be found), M valued as everyday lots; a lot that comes back above $250 an article is researched too.' Fix the Name N shots confirm in the same commit to say the room check and Agent Two follow by themselves.
findings.vnote: I captured the real confirm: 'Value 6 lines on this job? 4 researched against sold comparables, 2 valued as everyday lots…'. The count is taken before the $250-per-article ceiling re-sends, and a researched line with no sold comparable comes back as General estimate. The Name N shots sibling reads 'Nothing is valued and no disposition is set', while Agent Two in fact followed by itself in my run (1 agentValue call after the room check). The planner had already seen it.
